title: Everyday Life
description: Natural, high-frequency English for home, routines, shopping, cooking, free time, small talk and everyday problems.

items.definition: to wash the plates, cups, pans, etc. after a meal
items.example: I'll [do the dishes] if you put the kids to bed.
items.exampleRu: Я помою посуду, если ты уложишь детей спать.
items.trap: Not 'make the dishes' or 'clean the plates'; housework usually takes 'do': do the dishes, do the laundry, do the cleaning.

items.translation: заниматься мелкими делами, бегать по делам
items.definition: to go to different places to do small jobs such as shopping or going to the bank
items.example: I spent most of Saturday morning [running errands] around town.
items.exampleRu: Почти всё субботнее утро я бегал по городу по разным делам.
items.trap: Not 'do my affairs' (calque of «делать свои дела»); 'affairs' sounds formal or romantic.

items.definition: to make a place neat by putting things where they belong
items.example: Can you [tidy up] the living room before our guests arrive?
items.exampleRu: Можешь прибраться в гостиной до прихода гостей?
items.pattern: tidy (sth) up / tidy up after sb
items.trap: «Убираться» is usually 'tidy up' (put things away) or 'clean' (remove dirt), not 'clean up the room' for everyday tidying.

items.definition: to carry the bag of waste from your home to the bin outside
items.example: It's your turn to [take out the rubbish] tonight, not mine.
items.exampleRu: Сегодня твоя очередь выносить мусор, а не моя.
items.pattern: take the rubbish out / take out the rubbish
items.trap: Not 'carry out the garbage'. 'Rubbish' is British, 'trash/garbage' is American.

items.definition: to sleep longer than you intended and wake up late
items.example: I [overslept] this morning and missed my usual train.
items.exampleRu: Сегодня утром я проспал и опоздал на свою обычную электричку.
items.trap: Not 'sleep over' — that means to spend the night at someone's house. Past form is 'overslept'.

items.definition: to make a clock or phone ring at a particular time
items.example: Don't forget to [set an alarm] — our flight is at seven.
items.exampleRu: Не забудь поставить будильник — у нас вылет в семь.
items.trap: Not 'put an alarm' (calque of «поставить будильник»).

items.definition: to prepare yourself, for example by washing and dressing, before going somewhere
items.example: It usually takes me about twenty minutes to [get ready] for work.
items.exampleRu: Обычно мне нужно минут двадцать, чтобы собраться на работу.
items.pattern: get ready for sth / to do sth
items.trap: «Собираться» (prepare to go out) is 'get ready', not 'gather' or 'collect myself'.

items.translation: ездить на работу, дорога на работу
items.definition: to travel regularly between your home and your place of work; also the journey itself
items.example: I [commute] to the city centre by train, which takes about forty minutes.
items.exampleRu: Я езжу на работу в центр на электричке, дорога занимает минут сорок.
items.pattern: commute to/from + place; commute by train/car

items.definition: to keep doing things in the same regular order every day
items.example: It's surprisingly hard to [stick to a routine] when you work from home.
items.exampleRu: Когда работаешь из дома, на удивление трудно придерживаться режима.
items.trap: Not 'keep to the regime' — 'regime' in English is mainly political or medical.

items.definition: having very little money to spend
items.example: We're [on a tight budget] this month, so let's cook at home.
items.exampleRu: В этом месяце у нас с деньгами туго, так что давай готовить дома.
items.trap: Not 'with a small budget' in this sense; the fixed phrase uses 'on'.

items.translation: сравнивать цены, присматриваться в разных магазинах
items.definition: to compare prices or quality in different shops before buying something
items.example: It's worth [shopping around] before you buy a new fridge.
items.exampleRu: Прежде чем покупать новый холодильник, стоит сравнить цены в разных магазинах.

items.definition: available at a lower price than usual
items.example: These boots were [on sale], so I got them for half price.
items.exampleRu: Эти ботинки продавались со скидкой, так что я купила их за полцены.
items.trap: Don't confuse with 'for sale' — available to buy (e.g. a house for sale), with no discount implied.

items.definition: something that costs much more than it should
items.example: Twelve pounds for a sandwich at the station? That's a total [rip-off].
items.exampleRu: Двенадцать фунтов за бутерброд на вокзале? Это же просто грабёж.
items.trap: Informal; in formal complaints say 'overpriced' instead.

items.definition: to use all of something so that there is none left
items.example: We've [run out of] coffee again, so I'll add it to the shopping list.
items.exampleRu: У нас опять закончился кофе, добавлю его в список покупок.
items.pattern: sb runs out of sth / sth runs out
items.trap: The person is the subject: 'We've run out of milk', not 'Milk has run out of us'. Avoid 'The milk finished' (calque of «молоко закончилось»).

items.definition: to go out of a place for a short time, often to get something
items.example: I'm just going to [pop out] for some bread — back in ten minutes.
items.exampleRu: Я выскочу за хлебом — вернусь через десять минут.
items.pattern: pop out (for sth / to do sth)

items.definition: to not throw away the piece of paper that proves you paid for something
items.example: Make sure you [keep the receipt] in case the shirt doesn't fit.
items.exampleRu: Обязательно сохрани чек на случай, если рубашка не подойдёт.
items.trap: Not 'check' — in British English that's a mark (✓); in the US it means a restaurant bill. The 'p' in 'receipt' is silent.

items.definition: to receive your money back, for example after returning something to a shop
items.example: I took the broken kettle back and [got a refund] without any problems.
items.exampleRu: Я отнёс сломанный чайник обратно, и мне без проблем вернули деньги.
items.trap: Not 'return money back' (tautology). Say 'get a refund' or 'get my money back'.

items.definition: to put on clothes or shoes to see if they fit or look good
items.example: Can I [try on] this jacket in a bigger size, please?
items.exampleRu: Можно примерить этот пиджак на размер больше?
items.pattern: try sth on / try on sth
items.trap: Not 'measure' (calque of «мерить»). Also: 'fit' = right size, 'suit' = looks good on you.

items.definition: to cook something by doing exactly what the instructions say
items.example: I'm not a great cook, but I can [follow a recipe] if it's simple.
items.exampleRu: Я не очень хорошо готовлю, но по простому рецепту справлюсь.
items.trap: 'Recipe' is for cooking; a doctor's «рецепт» is a 'prescription'.

items.definition: to make food that has already been cooked hot again
items.example: I'll just [heat up] yesterday's soup for lunch.
items.exampleRu: На обед я просто разогрею вчерашний суп.
collocations: heat sth up in the microwave
items.pattern: heat sth up / heat up sth

items.definition: food that has not been eaten at the end of a meal and is kept for later
items.example: We had [leftovers] for dinner because nobody felt like cooking.
items.exampleRu: На ужин мы доели то, что осталось, потому что никому не хотелось готовить.
items.trap: Usually plural as a noun: 'leftovers'. As an adjective it is 'leftover' (leftover rice).

items.translation: заказать еду на дом, взять еду навынос
items.definition: to buy a cooked meal from a restaurant to eat at home
items.example: Let's just [order a takeaway] tonight — I'm too tired to cook.
items.exampleRu: Давай сегодня просто закажем еду — я слишком устала, чтобы готовить.
items.trap: 'Takeaway' is British; Americans say 'takeout'.

items.translation: есть вне дома, ходить в ресторан
items.definition: to have a meal in a restaurant or café instead of at home
items.example: We [eat out] about once a week, usually somewhere local.
items.exampleRu: Мы ходим в кафе примерно раз в неделю, обычно куда-нибудь поблизости.
items.trap: Not the same as 'eat outside' (= eat in the open air).

items.definition: a healthy combination of the different types of food your body needs
items.example: My doctor told me to eat [a balanced diet] with more vegetables.
items.exampleRu: Врач посоветовал мне питаться сбалансированно и есть больше овощей.
items.trap: 'Diet' means everything you usually eat, not only a weight-loss plan («диета»); for that say 'be on a diet'.

items.definition: to stay in bed later than usual in the morning, on purpose
items.example: On Sundays I usually [sleep in] until about ten.
items.exampleRu: По воскресеньям я обычно сплю примерно до десяти.
items.trap: Not 'oversleep' — 'sleep in' is deliberate, 'oversleep' is an accident.

items.definition: to spend time somewhere or with someone in a relaxed way
items.example: We often [hang out] at a café near the office after work.
items.exampleRu: После работы мы часто зависаем в кафе рядом с офисом.
items.pattern: hang out with sb / at a place
items.trap: Informal. For «гулять с друзьями» say 'hang out with friends', not 'walk with friends' (that means literally walking).

items.definition: to start doing a new activity, especially a hobby or sport
items.example: I've [taken up] yoga to help me deal with stress.
items.exampleRu: Я начала заниматься йогой, чтобы справляться со стрессом.
items.trap: Not 'begin to occupy myself with' (calque of «заниматься»).

items.definition: to relax after a period of work or stress
items.example: I need a hot bath and a good book to [unwind] after a long day.
items.exampleRu: Чтобы расслабиться после долгого дня, мне нужны горячая ванна и хорошая книга.
items.trap: Not 'relax myself' — 'unwind' and 'relax' are used without 'myself'.

items.definition: to meet or talk with someone and find out what has happened since you last met
items.example: It was really nice to [catch up with] Anna over coffee yesterday.
items.exampleRu: Вчера было здорово посидеть с Анной за кофе и поболтать о новостях.
items.pattern: catch up with sb / catch up on sth

items.translation: вести светскую беседу, болтать о пустяках
items.definition: to have a polite conversation about unimportant things such as the weather
items.example: I find it hard to [make small talk] with neighbours I barely know.
items.exampleRu: Мне трудно болтать о пустяках с соседями, которых я почти не знаю.
items.trap: Not 'do small talk' or 'speak small talk'. 'Small talk' is uncountable: not 'a small talk'.

items.definition: an informal way of saying hello and asking how someone is
items.example: Hi Tom, [how's it going]? I haven't seen you for ages.
items.exampleRu: Привет, Том, как жизнь? Сто лет тебя не видел.
collocations: what have you been up to?
items.trap: It's a greeting, not a real question: answer briefly ('Good, thanks — you?'), not with a detailed report.

items.definition: an informal reply meaning that things are fine
items.example: "How are things?" "[Can't complain], thanks — work's busy but good."
items.exampleRu: «Как дела?» — «Грех жаловаться, спасибо. На работе завал, но всё хорошо».

items.definition: used to introduce a new topic or extra information in a conversation
items.example: [By the way], did you see the email from our landlord?
items.exampleRu: Кстати, ты видел письмо от нашего арендодателя?
items.trap: Only for «кстати» as a topic change; «очень кстати» (= at the right moment) is 'just in time' or 'that's handy'.

items.definition: if a machine or vehicle breaks down, it stops working
items.example: Our washing machine [broke down] in the middle of a wash.
items.exampleRu: Наша стиральная машина сломалась прямо посреди стирки.
items.trap: Use 'break down' for machines and cars; for objects like a cup or a phone screen use 'break'.

items.definition: if a container or pipe leaks, liquid or gas comes out through a hole or crack
items.example: There's water all over the kitchen floor — I think a pipe is [leaking].
items.exampleRu: Весь пол на кухне в воде — кажется, протекает труба.
items.trap: Not 'flow' (calque of «течь») — 'flow' is for rivers or traffic, not broken pipes.

items.definition: to arrange for someone else to repair something for you
items.example: I need to [get my phone fixed] because the screen is cracked.
items.exampleRu: Мне нужно отдать телефон в ремонт — экран треснул.
items.trap: 'I fixed my phone' means you did it yourself; if a repair shop did it, say 'I got my phone fixed'.

items.definition: a period when the electricity supply stops
items.example: We had a [power cut] last night, so we ate by candlelight.
items.exampleRu: Вчера вечером отключили свет, так что мы ужинали при свечах.
items.trap: For «отключили свет» say 'there was a power cut' or 'the power went off', not 'they turned off the light'.

items.definition: to accidentally close a door that locks and leave your keys inside
items.example: I [locked myself out] last week and had to call a locksmith.
items.exampleRu: На прошлой неделе я захлопнул дверь без ключей, и пришлось вызывать слесаря.

items.definition: to be unable to move forward because there are too many vehicles on the road
items.example: Sorry I'm late — I [got stuck in traffic] on the ring road.
items.exampleRu: Извините за опоздание — застрял в пробке на кольцевой.
items.trap: Not 'stand in a traffic jam' (calque of «стоять в пробке»); 'traffic' is uncountable: not 'a traffic' or 'traffics'.

items.definition: if a public machine or device is out of order, it is not working
items.example: The lift is [out of order] again, so we had to take the stairs.
items.exampleRu: Лифт опять не работает, так что пришлось идти пешком.
collocations: the ticket machine is out of order
items.trap: Used mainly for public machines (lifts, ticket machines, toilets); for your own laptop say 'it's not working'.
